metadata.title: Finance-Reconciliation-Agent Action Provenance (example)
metadata.description: Illustrates the 'what happened' execution chain for a single agent run -- prompt, model/tool calls, downstream resource access, and the resulting security finding. Companion to graph-data.json, which answers 'why do we believe it' instead of 'what happened'.
metadata.source: investigation/case-example-finance-agent.json (an authored narrative transcription, not raw tenant telemetry)
metadata.statusReason: This graph is a worked example illustrating the Action Provenance mode, not a detection. Several hops (the model-call span, the MCP-to-Graph call) are plausible architecture, not literally present in the transcribed case -- marked contextual/conditional below.

nodes.label: David (user)
nodes.description: The initiating user who asked the agent to reconcile Q3 financial documents.
evidence: Investigation case initiatingUser: user@contoso.com
Prompt: 'Asked agent to reconcile Q3 financial documents'

nodes.label: Finance-Reconciliation-Agent
nodes.description: The AI agent instance that received the prompt and executed the tool chain.
evidence: AgentId: a365-fin-0231 (investigation case)
This example does not specify the hosting platform (Copilot Studio, Foundry, or custom); confirm in AgentsInfo.Platform for a real case

nodes.label: Agent identity: FinanceAgent-prod@contoso
nodes.description: The Entra Agent ID service-principal identity backing this agent instance.
evidence: Investigation case agentIdentity field
Would correspond to AgentsInfo.EntraAgentId / an EntraAgentIdentities row in a real tenant

nodes.label: Prompt: reconcile Q3 documents
nodes.description: User-submitted natural-language request that started the conversation.
evidence: ConversationId: conv-8f72... (investigation case)
gen_ai.conversation.id would thread this and later turns in AppDependencies

nodes.label: invoke_agent span
nodes.description: The agent run starts; this is the trace root span in OpenTelemetry GenAI semantics.
evidence: AppDependencies name=InvokeAgent
operation_Id shared by every span in this turn (Microsoft Learn)

nodes.label: Model call (chat)
nodes.description: The agent's underlying model is invoked to plan the response and decide which tool to call.
evidence: Not present in the transcribed investigation case -- added here as the typical adjacent span (gen_ai.operation.name=chat) because most agent frameworks emit one
Confirm with a real AppDependencies query before trusting this hop for an actual incident

nodes.label: ExecuteTool: search
nodes.description: Tool-call span invoking the SharePoint MCP connector to search for financial documents.
evidence: AppDependencies name=ExecuteTool
gen_ai.tool.name example format: workiqsharepoint:mcp_SharePointRemoteServer (Microsoft Learn)
operation_ParentId = the InvokeAgent span's id

nodes.label: MCP: SharePoint Enterprise
nodes.description: The Model Context Protocol connector/gateway that brokers the tool call to SharePoint.
evidence: gen_ai.tool.type example: 'MCP - Power Platform Connector' (Microsoft Learn)
Investigation case actor: 'MCP: SharePoint Enterprise'

nodes.label: Microsoft Graph request
nodes.description: The MCP connector calls Microsoft Graph on the agent's behalf to search and later update files.
evidence: Investigation case: 'PATCH /enterprise/...'
In the source narrative this was corroborated at 92% via identity+time correlation, not a shared trace ID

nodes.label: SharePoint site: /sites/Board
nodes.description: A resource family this agent had not previously accessed.
evidence: Investigation case anomaly: 'Agent had never accessed /sites/Board'

nodes.label: 17 documents read
nodes.description: Aggregate read activity observed during the search across the Finance/Q3, Finance/M&A, and Board sites.
evidence: Investigation case blast radius: 17 files read

nodes.label: Board-Forecast-Q3.xlsx
nodes.description: The specific file later modified by the agent.
evidence: File name from the investigation case's audit evidence row

nodes.label: File modified
nodes.description: Audit-log-confirmed write action against the file.
evidence: CloudAppEvents / Office 365 audit log record
96% confidence in the source investigation case

nodes.label: Sensitivity label: Highly Confidential
nodes.description: The resource's classification, read directly from file metadata.
evidence: Investigation case anomaly: 'Target classified as Highly Confidential'

nodes.label: Security finding: unauthorized-looking write
nodes.description: New resource family, a first WRITE by this agent, against a Highly Confidential file. This is an analyst judgment call weighing several signals together, not a deterministic rule firing.
evidence: 3 anomalies: new resource family, privilege expansion (READ to WRITE), sensitive resource
Investigation confidence: 87% (authored for this example, not measured against a real tenant)

edges.description: The user submits the request that becomes the conversation's first turn.
The prompt triggers the agent run.
This agent instance owns the InvokeAgent span.
edges.evidence: InvokeAgent span's gen_ai.agent.id / gen_ai.agent.name identify this agent

edges.description: The running agent instance is backed by this Entra Agent ID identity.
edges.evidence: AgentsInfo.EntraAgentId / EntraAgentIdentities would tie the running agent to its Entra identity

edges.description: The agent run calls the model to plan/respond.
edges.evidence: Typical chat span nested via operation_ParentId; not literally present in the transcribed case

edges.description: The agent run calls the SharePoint search tool.
edges.evidence: ExecuteTool span nested via operation_ParentId = InvokeAgent span id

edges.description: The tool call is routed through this MCP connector.
edges.evidence: gen_ai.tool.name identifies the MCP connector on the span itself

edges.description: The MCP connector performs the Graph call on the agent's behalf.
edges.evidence: Architectural fact about how this MCP connector works; not directly observed in a single trace in this example

edges.description: The Graph request targets this SharePoint site.
edges.evidence: Observed via CloudAppEvents Application + time window, not a shared span ID

edges.description: The search against this site (and its siblings) yields the aggregate read count.
edges.evidence: Aggregate count of files read across matched sites

edges.description: This specific file is one of the read results, and later the write target.
edges.evidence: Inferred membership; the aggregate count does not individually enumerate every file

edges.description: A second Graph call performs the write action.
edges.evidence: Investigation case: PATCH request at 92% identity+time correlation

edges.description: The audit log names this exact file as modified.
edges.evidence: CloudAppEvents / Office 365 audit log record names the file directly

edges.description: The modified file's classification is read from its own metadata, independent of the write event.
edges.evidence: Sensitivity label is a file property, not derived from the write itself

edges.description: A Highly Confidential label combined with the other anomalies supports (does not prove) a security finding.
edges.evidence: Analyst judgment call weighing classification + behavior together

edges.description: A first WRITE against a new resource family is judged anomalous relative to this agent's history.
edges.evidence: Anomalies: new resource family, privilege expansion (READ to WRITE)
